tomes.description_cn: 作者“红花女士”在本书中讲述了受兰开斯特家族青睐的，又名“日落之路”的炼金学技艺。这些技艺使他们在路权战争中取得最终胜利，却又被描述为“现已衰落”。

readings.intro: The generals of the Houses of Lancaster and York are described as 'brother-enemies' - a term more usually associated with the dyadic, invariably twinned Edge-long…
readings.content: The author's conclusion is that in the absence of the operations of the Dawn Road, the operations of Sunset inevitably became unbalanced, debased, and ultimately enfeebled. The combination of the two is described, tantalisingly, as 'the Forge's True Alloy'.

readings_cn.content: 作者的结论是，如果没有拂晓之路，日落之路也会不可避免地失衡、衰弱，最终走向倾颓。两者的结合被诱人地描述为“铸炉的真正合金”。
readings_cn.intro: 兰开斯特家族和约克家族的领袖们被描述为“兄敌”，一个常与对立双刃——惯为成双的刃之长生者有联系的词汇……

tomes.name: Lady Eva's Repose
tomes.description: A 'meditation' on the drowning of Lady Eva Dewulf and her two grandchildren, written in the years when the estate was abandoned by Father Theo, once the Dewulf family chaplain, one of the few to remain on the Isle in those desolate years.
tomes.description_cn: 一部对伊娃·德沃尔夫女士和她两个孙女溺亡的“沉思录”，写于庄园被遗弃的时代。作者西奥神父曾是德沃尔夫家族的牧师，是那段荒凉岁月里留在岛上的少数人之一。

readings.intro: 'There are so many stories of her heritage, so many rumours of her persistence. We might easily choose to believe that the grand-twins escaped - even that they live yet beyond the sea - '
readings.content: Father Theo has come to believe that Eva sought an escape from a family curse - the 'pale heritage' of Hafren her forebear, or the curse placed upon the line by the cunning-man Red William in the time of Hendrik Dewulf. He had begun by believing neither curse was real; but as the book concludes, he decides that he has determined to believe in them, rather than accept the three deaths as a futile tragedy. 'One does not so easily escape the long necessity of faith,' he concludes.

readings_cn.intro: “有太多关于她遗产的故事，有太多关于她生还的传闻。我们更倾向于相信那对孪生孙女逃过一劫——甚至认定她们仍然生活在海洋彼端……”
readings_cn.content: 西奥神父开始相信，伊娃是为了摆脱家族的诅咒——她的祖先哈芙伦的“苍白遗产”，或者是亨德里克·德沃尔夫时期神汉红威廉对家族施加的诅咒。他在开篇认为这两个诅咒都子虚乌有；但在本书结尾，他决定宁可信其有，而不是把三人的死亡视作一场徒劳的悲剧。“摆脱对信仰的长期依赖并不那么容易，”他总结道。

tomes.name: Operations of a Certain Finality
tomes.description: Subtitled 'The Hammer's Sundering'. The work of an anonymous adept who violently despised the Invisible Serapeum, the library of the Watchman's Tree in Alexandria.
tomes.description_cn: 副标题为“锤之分裂”。作者未知，但毫无疑问是位学徒，他极度鄙夷隐形的塞拉皮雍，那座位于亚历山大港的守夜人之树图书馆。

readings.intro: The author outlines the means they had taken to sabotage the place and its collection, which increasingly seem more poetic than effective, to the point where the whole business may in fact be some kind of allegory.
readings.content: The author gloats that with the techniques of Putrefaction and Calcination, they have transformed the Library's stocks of asimel to 'a seduction of black sapphire' which will ensure the texts therein contain only 'Moon-truths'.

readings_cn.intro: 作者概述了自己用来破坏那座图书馆和其中馆藏的方法，但这些方法越读越发显得诗意而不是有效，以至于让人怀疑，书中的内容实际上可能是某种隐喻。
readings_cn.content: 作者得意洋洋地说，通过“腐化与煅烧”技术，自己已经把图书馆的所有阿苏麦库存转变成了“黑刚玉的诱惑”，这将确保用之写下的文本只包含“月之真理”。

tomes.name: The Alloy of the White Rose
tomes.description: An account by 'Mistress White-Flower' of the alchemical techniques favoured by the House of York, also identified with the 'Dawn Road'. These techniques failed to bring them victory in the War of the Roads, but are 'not to be discounted'.
tomes.description_cn: 作者“白花女士”在本书中讲述了受约克家族青睐的，又名“拂晓之路”的炼金学技术。这些技术未能使得他们在路权战争中取得胜利，但也“不可忽视其作用”。

readings.intro: The author asserts proudly that the Dawn Road ends in the Second Dawn; and hints darkly that the downfall of the House of York was 'Grail-sabotage'.
readings.content: 'Mistress White-Flower' urges a 'History of Uzult', where the Second Dawn may come to pass. She identifies Xanthotic Essence as Uzult's predecessor; she explains that with sufficient Lantern, Bitterblack Salts can be Purified to Xanthotic Essence, and Iotic Essence can be Exalted to Xanthotic Essence.

readings_cn.content: “白花女士”力求人们了解“珀金写就的历史”，在这重历史中第二拂晓可能会实现。她指出，黄化精华是珀金的前体；她解释道，只要有足够的灯，便能将苦黑盐提纯为黄化精华，或是将赤化精华转变为黄化精华。
readings_cn.intro: 作者自豪地宣称，拂晓之路的终点是第二拂晓；并隐晦地暗示约克家族的没落是由于“圣杯的蓄意破坏”。

tomes.name: Ud Rocashaas
tomes.description: An anonymous confessional account of unsanctioned activities by the nuns of St Brandan's. The title is a Henavek phrase that might be translated as 'the spirit flees the shadowed places.'
tomes.description_cn: 一本匿名的忏悔录，记录了圣布伦丹的修女们所做的未经批准的行为。标题是一个赫沃尔语短句，可以翻译成“心灵逃离覆影之地”。

readings.intro: The author writes guiltily of her dealings with hill-children and Carapace-relics - she suggests she herself has a connection with one of the Carapace-kinds. Most of these dealings are trivial, but she claims to have arranged the death of the Marcher Lord William de Braose, called Black William...
readings.content: De Braose' wife, Eva, evidently seeks the Abbey's help to free her from her hated husband. Subsequently he is found in the bed-chamber of the wife of Llywelyn the Great, Prince of the Welsh, while attempting to negotiate the marriage of his daughter (also Eva) to Llywelyn's son. Llywellyn takes this badly, de Braose is hanged, the elder Eva inherits his estates and makes a substantial endowment to St Brandan's. In the author's telling, de Braose was 'innocent of all but cruelty' and the adulterer found in the bed-chamber was a shape-changing 'undergoer'...

readings_cn.intro: 作者语带歉疚地写到她与丘陵之子和介壳遗族的交易——她暗示自己仍与介壳种的某个种群保持联系。这些交易大多无关紧要，但她声称是自己筹划了边地领主威廉·德·布劳斯的死亡，即人称“黑威廉”的那位……
readings_cn.content: 德·布劳斯的妻子，伊娃，显然曾向修道院寻求帮助，好摆脱她那烦人的丈夫。随后，他就在威尔士亲王卢埃林妻子的卧室里被捉奸在床，当时布劳斯正在筹划女儿（也名叫伊娃）与卢埃林儿子的婚事。卢埃林勃然大怒，把德·布劳斯绞死了。年长的那位伊娃继承了布劳斯的财产，并向圣布伦丹修道院捐赠了一笔巨款。在作者的叙述中，德·布劳斯“除了残忍之外，在这件事里清清白白”，卧室里的通奸者只是个易形的“衾下魅”……

tomes.name: Unhatched Hymns
tomes.description: Hymns attributed to Saint Lucia the Eyeless, patron of glassworkers and Name of the Hour called Meniscate.
tomes.description_cn: 献给“无眼”圣露西亚的赞美诗，她是玻璃工匠的主保圣人，也是被称为弧月的司辰的具名者。

readings.intro: The hymns venerate every sanctioned Hour, celebrating them as the Sun Undivided, but also suggesting that each Hour may become the next - Madrugad to Watchman, Watchman to Wolf, and so on.
readings.content: The Hymn of the Phases celebrates the Meniscate 'from whom we do not turn', for the truth which is beauty, the beauty which is truth, and the perfect balance between the two. The Hymn of the Reflections, more puzzlingly, celebrates the Meniscate as the 'Sister of Janus, Mother of Shadow', whose 'visage wondrous in emptiness' can reveal all truths.

readings_cn.content: 《月相赞美诗》赞颂了弧月的“光彩夺目”，因为她的真即是美，美即是真，二者间达到了完美的平衡。更令人费解的是，《映照赞美诗》赞颂弧月是“雅努斯的姐妹，阴影的母亲”，她“空无一物的奇异面庞”可以揭示一切真理。
readings_cn.intro: 这些赞美诗赞颂每一位被承认的司辰，把祂们当作未分裂的太阳崇敬，但也暗示每一位司辰都可能转变为下一位——从昕旦到守夜人，守夜人到狼，以此类推。

tomes.name: An Echo of Silence
tomes.description: A very heterodox history of the House of Lethe as recorded by 'the Serenity' - a Lethean adept who declares that the House of Lethe was created explicitly to prevent the ascension of any more mortals to Name or Hour status.
tomes.description_cn: 对遗忘家族历史的一段相当非正统的叙述，作者自称“静谧者”；作为遗忘家族的一员，他宣称遗忘家族自建立起的目的就是阻止更多的凡人晋升至具名者，乃至司辰之位。

readings.intro: 'Eternity cannot be escaped; but in History, it may be delayed,' the Serenity explains. 'The gods-who-were-flesh, by their nature, are a surrender to Eternity.'
readings.content: The 'roots of the House' are said to pass into the Wood of dreams through three forests in the Bounds, identified as the Bei Ilai, the Black Cedar Forest, and the Brecheliant. 'While one tree of these may yet stand, one single tree, the Histories continue.'

readings_cn.content: 据说“居屋的根须”通过边境的三座森林深扎于梦境中的林地，分别是贝·伊莱、黑杉林和布劳赛良德森林。“只要它们中仍有一棵树木伫立不倒，只需一棵，诸史便能延续。”
readings_cn.intro: “永恒无可回避；但在历史中它或可被推迟，”静谧者解释道，“肉源诸神，究其本质，都是对永恒的屈服。”

tomes.name: Observations on the Peacock Door
tomes.description: Ninegala of Lagash discusses the Peacock Door, the highest door available to mortals in the Mansus: 'a rent, an imperfection, an abrasion.'
tomes.description_cn: 拉格什的宁娜伽勒探讨了孔雀之门——凡人在漫宿中能抵达的至高之门：“一种裂缝，一道瑕疵，一处磨损。”

readings.intro: Notably, the book is written in Vak, which by some accounts is another aspect of the Peacock Door itself. Ninegala addresses this by apologising courteously to the Door, and the language, at the end of every section.
readings.content: The Peacock Door did not exist - Ninegala says - in the days when the gods-from-stone entered the Mansus. They used the 'Fanged Key' to open the Savage Door, a door not usually available to mortals. 'Speech, as the initiates of Chione would have it, is a wound. I fear that through that wound, the blood of the Mansus flows even now, and that one day Speech will be an end to Dream. I fear that; but I fear the alternative far more.'

readings_cn.intro: 值得注意的是，这本书是用伐诃写就的，这据说是孔雀之门自身的另一面相。就此，在每一章节的结尾，宁娜伽勒都向这扇门扉和这门语言彬彬有礼地致歉。
readings_cn.content: 宁娜伽勒称：在石源神进入漫宿的时代，孔雀之门并不存在。祂们用“獠牙之钥”开启了凡人通常无法开启的狂暴之门。“正如喀俄涅的门徒所言，言辞即是伤口。令我担忧的是，经此伤口，漫宿的血流淌至今，终有一日，言辞将终结梦境。我担心此事；但我更担心另一种情况。”

tomes.name: The Ascendant
tomes.description: The Edge-long Dardesh boasts of her victories over her brother-enemy Tareg in the days of the Shadowless Empire.
tomes.description_cn: 刃之长生者丹德什夸耀了自己在无影帝国时期，与她的“兄敌”塔格的战争中取得的一系列胜利。

readings.intro: 'Sweeter than wine, than nectar is the blood of my brother. We have raised up armies one against another, we have sated the Blackbone with the sinking of our ships…'
readings.content: Dardesh's boasting at length turns melancholy. An Edge-long is half a dyad; she may not defeat her hated brother-enemy without ending herself. She doesn't even want to; but she is aware, to her frustration, that she is 'a piece on the board, an axle on the ox-cart' - an essential part of the eternal engine of contention which the Lionsmith and Colonel use to sustain the world.

readings_cn.intro: “比酒更甜、比蜜更甜的，是我兄弟的鲜血。我们召集军队彼此攻击。我们击沉对方的船只，使黑骸餍足……”
readings_cn.content: 丹德什的自夸最终转变为忧郁。一位刃之长生者是对刃的一半；如果不结束自己的生命，她就不可能打败她所讨厌的兄敌。她甚至不想这么做；而令她沮丧的是，她最终意识到自己不过是“棋盘上的棋子，牛车上的车轴”——是狮子匠和上校那永恒纷争引擎用来维系世界的基本组成部分。

tomes.name: The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manuscript)
tomes.name_cn: 《三者与三者》（凯尔伊苏姆抄本）
tomes.description: A more recent version of a much older text, this book describes the operations of the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. It has been heavily censored, but even so contains potent secrets.
tomes.description_cn: 一本古老书籍的新近版本，描述了圣坛和根冠的运作方式。它们分别由三位司辰组成，有着隐晦而广泛的权力和责任。这本书经过了严格的审查，但仍蕴含着强大的秘密。

readings.intro: 'The deepest knowledge is safeguarded by the Covenant of the Watchman's Tree, whose patrons are Calyptra - the three flowers on the Watchman's Tree - blood, soot, and snow…'
readings.content: Calyptra may be known, as Night, Dawn, Eclipse. The Chancel may be known, as Threshold, Mirror, Shell. Calyptra and Chancel then are two: is Janus a third?'

readings_cn.intro: “最深奥的知识受到守夜人之树盟约的保护，盟约的守护者是根冠——守夜人之树上的三朵花——血，灰，与雪……”
readings_cn.content: “已知根冠可为黑夜，拂晓，日蚀。圣坛可为门关，镜子，贝壳。根冠与圣坛仅为二者：雅努斯是否是第三者？”

tomes.name: The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscript)
tomes.description: A Church-authorised version of an older text, this book describes the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. It has clearly been reworked to fit Church doctrine.
tomes.description_cn: 一本古老书籍的教会审査版，描述了圣坛和根冠的运作方式。它们分别由三位司辰组成，有着隐晦而广泛的权力和责任。这个版本显然是为了贴合教义而重新编写的。

readings.intro: 'The deepest knowledge is forbidden to all mortals except those who seek it beneath the Watchman's Tree. It is Calyptra that planted that tree, but it is the Chancel, the Cruciate, that has elected Calyptra. Who then elected the Cruciate? Or is this, as the saying goes, 'a matter of Janus'?
readings.content: 'The Sister-and-Witch is Cruciate, but the Witch-and-Sister is not. Even those powers that demand a conjunction are not always conjoined. When the Sister is Nowhere, does this mean Nowhere sits in crucem?'

readings_cn.intro: “除了那些在守夜人之树下求索者，最深奥的知识对所有凡人都是禁忌。是根冠培植了此树，但却是圣坛，也即圣十字决定了根冠的人选。而又是谁决定了圣十字的人选？亦或者正如俗语所说，‘事关雅努斯’？”
readings_cn.content: “双生巫女是圣十字的成员，而双生女巫则不然。即使是司掌结合的神灵也不总是结合在一起。那当巫女位于虚界时，是否意味着虚界位于十字之中？”

tomes.name: The Other Eye of the Serpent
tomes.description: In which the heresiarch Cygnifer attempts to resolve certain mysteries of Lightning.
tomes.description_cn: 异端学者希格尼法在本书中试图解开关于闪电的某些谜团。

readings.intro: Cygnifer considers Lightning to be 'the division, the connection, the joined serpent.' The Serpent's Eye is said to be the Sun - but as the division and connection, it must have a second Eye.
readings.content: Cygnifer considers and rejects, three times, the hypothesis that the Moon is the Serpent's other eye, insisting that it and the Sun do not share a nature. (This, as much as the Serpent business, is what got him burnt by the Church.) He proposes that the Serpent's teeth are towers, that the Serpent's mouth is a gate, that the Serpent is the 'devourer of Ys'... and 'therefore' that the Serpent's other eye is amber.

readings_cn.intro: 希格尼法认为闪电是“分裂，连接，弥合的蛇”。蛇的一只眼睛据称是太阳——但正如分裂与连接一般，它必然还有第二只眼。
readings_cn.content: 希格尼法曾三度考虑月亮是蛇的另一只眼睛的假设，但又三度否认了这点，并坚持认为它与太阳间缺乏共性。（这件事与他对蛇的研究都是导致他被教会烧死的原因。）他推测蛇的牙齿是塔楼，而它的嘴是门关，而蛇本身是“伊苏的吞噬者”……“因而”，蛇的另一只眼睛是琥珀。

tomes.name: On Imperfections
tomes.description: Poemander, light-smith and Lantern-long, describes the process of 'transinhabitation', which he calls 'a manifestation of imperfection.'
tomes.description_cn: 光匠兼灯之长生者——“牧人者”在本文中描述了“转居”的过程，他称之为“有瑕疵的显灵”。

readings.intro: Lantern-long lack bodies, and so cannot normally leave the Mansus - but they can 'steady-glint' in the physical world by establishing a 'road of glass'. Poemander notes with disgust that the order of Long called the Obliviates refer to it as 'scrining', which he considers a 'debased term'.
readings.content: Poemander explains the benefits of transinhabitation - that a Lantern-long can affect the senses and thoughts of those nearby, that they can even enter their spirits, and that they can 'employ the senses of those inhabited to experience again the scent of blossom and season'. This seems to be what interests him most. He insists that a Lantern-long should only ever inhabit a mirror of silver, not silvered glass, but he declines to explain why.

readings_cn.content: “牧人者”阐述了“转居”的种种好处：灯之长生者可以影响周围人的感官与思想，甚至可以进入他们的灵魂，这让其能“利用宿主的感官再次体验鲜花和时节的气味”。这似乎是他最感兴趣的地方。他还坚持认为灯之长生者只能栖居在银镜里，而不是镀银玻璃中，却并没有解释原因。
readings_cn.intro: 灯之长生者没有肉体，所以无法正常地离开漫宿——但是他们能够通过建立一条“玻璃之路”，在现实世界中“稳定地闪烁”。“牧人者”厌恶地注释道，有个名为忘却会的长生者团体更喜欢将之称为“附体”——他认为这是个“贬义词”。

results.result_name_cn: 教诲：玻璃吹制与容器制造

tomes.name: The Secret Colours
tomes.description: Black Elie, disgraced Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot, wrote this while fleeing the 'agents of the Duty.'
tomes.description_cn: 黑艾丽，大马士革的三重绳结姐妹会名誉扫地的女头领，在逃避“当局的特务”期间写下了本书。

readings.intro: Elie writes of the 'secret colours of the Sun' - the blessed 'traces of Error' - weaknesses in sunlight, balancing principles in its reflection.
readings.content: A deeper account of these secret colours, Elie reveals, was kept at a shrine to the Three Hours of the Chancel at the 'grey rock in the sea', far from the intrigues of Sisterhood and Church. It is hidden from the common eye, but can be revealed with the arts of Sickle and Eclipse.

readings_cn.intro: 艾丽提到“太阳的秘密色彩”——被赐福的“错误痕迹”——阳光中的弱点，它倒影中的平衡准则。
readings_cn.content: 艾丽透露道，关于这些秘密色彩更为深入的描述，被藏在了位于“海中灰岩”之上，圣坛三司辰的神龛中，远离了姐妹会与教会的阴谋。寻常的注视看不见它，但可以用“镰刀与日蚀”之技艺将其揭露。

tomes.name: Deaths and their Evasions
tomes.description: Father Stanislav John Schaller writes of the means and limitation of passage between the orders of the Mansus - Know, Long, Names, Hours. Unusually, Father John has written this book in Fucine - for, he says, especial secrecy.
tomes.description_cn: 斯坦尼斯拉夫·约翰·沙勒神父在本书中写了在漫宿中的各层级——通晓者、长生者、具名者与司辰间晋升的方法与限制。约翰神父罕见地使用了富奇诺语——据他所说，是专门为了保密。

readings.intro: He speaks very cautiously of the exceptions that can sometimes be made to the edicts of Chancel and Calyptra, and hints at the means by which he successfully returned a Lantern-long to flesh...
readings.content: Schaller mentions most cautiously of all that he has been permitted to see a book that speaks more deeply on the matter, but that it was surrendered 'into the shadow of a covenant-stone of the Watchman's Tree.' It can be retrieved if 'the ninety-ninth wink is reserved under the Edicts Liminal.'

readings_cn.content: 沙勒慎之又慎地提到，他曾受许借阅一本更深入地探讨了这个主题的书，但它被藏在了“守夜人之树的盟约石”的阴影之中。如果“用‘阈限之敕令’留存住第九十九次眨眼”，就能再次找到它。
readings_cn.intro: 他非常谨慎地谈到，圣坛与根冠的敕令有时也会出现例外，而且隐晦地暗示了他如何成功使一位灯之长生者重获肉体……

tomes.name: A Tower Falls
tomes.description: The phonograph is packaged in glossy amethyst purple card with the words A TOWER FALLS in nine languages on both sides. There is no other identifying information at all.
tomes.description_cn: 录音带被收纳在紫水晶制成的紫色反光盒中，包装盒的两面用九种语言写着“塔之倒坍”的字样。没有其他可用于识别的信息。

readings.intro: A recording of uncertain origin: inexplicably compelling poetry recorded by a speaker with a rasping, rumbling, impossibly deep voice… in the language called Vak, which probably isn't spoken by more than a few dozen living scholars.
readings.content: The poem speaks of a four-winged war, a four-mouthed king, a four-rayed sun, a four-cornered stone. It speaks of a tide-washed hunger of the heart; it speaks, lastly, of its own conclusion, when it might, might, might be spoken in dreams before the Deep Door, by a Messenger of Histories...

readings_cn.content: 诗歌讲述了四翼之战，四口之王，四射之日，四角之岩。它诉说了内心被潮水冲刷的渴望；最后，它说出了自己的结论：它或许，只是或许，仅仅只是或许，会被一名诸史的送信人，在深邃之门前的梦境中说出……
readings_cn.intro: 一段来源不明的录音：用名为伐诃的语言——在世的学者中，理解这种语言的可能不超过十指之数——录制的莫名引人入胜的诗歌。话者的嗓音如雷鸣般隆隆作响，沙哑、低沉得难以置信……

tomes.name: A Tower Rises
tomes.description: The phonograph is packaged in glossy card the bright pink of a dog-rose, with the words A TOWER RISES in nine languages on both sides. There is no other identifying information at all.
tomes.description_cn: 录音带被收纳在犬蔷薇般的亮粉色反光盒中，包装盒的两面用九种语言写着“塔之攀升”的字样。没有其他可供识别的信息。

readings.intro: A recording of uncertain origin: inexplicably compelling poetry recorded by a speaker with a high, sweet voice that scales up beyond human hearing… in the language called Vak, which probably isn't spoken by more than a few dozen living scholars.
readings.content: The poem speaks of the Wheel that turns, the Coil that turns, the Tide that returns, Egg that returns; it speaks of a cloven sky, an opened heart, a dream of glittering eyes; speaks, lastly, of its own conclusion, when it might, might, might be spoken in dreams before the Deep Door, by a Messenger of Histories...

readings_cn.intro: 一段来源不明的录音：用名为伐诃的语言——在世的学者中，理解这种语言的可能不超过十指之数——录制的莫名引人入胜的诗歌。话者的嗓音高亢，甜美，几乎超出了人类的听阈……
readings_cn.content: 诗歌讲述了转动之轮，转扭之蟠，回返之潮，回归之卵。它诉说了破碎的天空，敞开的心灵，闪烁眼睛的梦；最后，它说出了自己的结论：它或许，只是或许，仅仅只是或许，会被一名诸史的送信人，在深邃之门前的梦境中说出……

tomes.name: The Chandler's Wish
tomes.description: Formulae and instructions invoking Moth, Lantern and - exceptionally, paradoxically - the liminal and theoretical Hour called the Chandler. The author is anonymous, admitting only that they are 'one who is not yet nameless.'
tomes.description_cn: 本书中的公式和阐释唤起了蛾与灯——还罕见而矛盾地拜请了临界态的、理论中的司辰——制烛人。作者不愿透露自己的姓名，只承认自己是一个“尚未无名之人”。

readings.intro: The author makes a passionate argument that the Hour named Chandler is in fact the oldest, even though he does not exist, because he is - supposedly - the culminating event of a plan that precedes even Grail and Moth.
readings.content: 'Where the Chandler has passed, the understandings of the Colonel and the Lionsmith will wrench open truth. Where the Chandler will pass, Moth will pass before him.'

readings_cn.content: “制烛人已到之处，上校和狮子匠相互理解的协定将揭开真幕。制烛人将过之途，蛾将先他一步。”
readings_cn.intro: 作者热情洋溢地论证道，名为制烛人的司辰实际上是最古老的，尽管他并不存在，因为据称他是某个计划的最终结果，而该计划甚至先于圣杯与飞蛾而存在。

tomes.name: Sunset Celia and the End of Days
tomes.description: An Obliviate adept identified only as 'the Emiliano' rants desperately about the part Sunset Celia played in the Intercalate, as 'the proxy of the Sun'.
tomes.description_cn: 一位人称“埃米利亚诺”的忘却会学徒绝望地怒斥了日落西莉亚在置闰中扮演的角色——“太阳的代理人”。

readings.intro: 'Now she walks behind the Watchman, but did she always? She has many of the characteristics of a Maid-in-the-Mirror, after all. In older texts she has been called Caelia the Elagabaline. Perhaps she was his daughter? Perhaps Tryphon's sister? Perhaps, like the Watchman himself, she is like a shadow cast by two candles.'
readings.content: 'What must be revealed, will be revealed. Our Order's root is tainted, but its branches flourish beneath the shelter of the Watchman's greater Tree. I shall invoke its rites before the Chancel, the Cruciate, and the Rode. I shall write a final History. Or another shall write it for me.'

readings_cn.intro: “如今她行在守夜人的身后，但她是否一向如此？毕竟她有许多镜中少女的特征。在更古老的文献中她被称为埃拉伽巴路斯的赛莉亚。也许她是他的女儿？也许她是特里丰的姊妹？也许，就如守夜人本人一样，她就像两根蜡烛投下的影子。”
readings_cn.content: “该揭露的终将被揭露。我们教团的根基已被玷污，但其分支在守夜人之树下仍枝繁叶茂。我将在圣坛，在圣屏，在圣十字前举行它的仪式。我将会写下最后的历史。或由他人代我写下。”

tomes.name: The Carmine Petal: Revised
tomes.description: An apparently theoretical project proposed by 'Lionel' of the Society of the Noble Endeavour which might permit the imprisonment of a renegade Forge-Name. A very heavily revised edition of an earlier and even more controversial work.
tomes.description_cn: 一份也许停留在理论层面的计划书，由高贵之举社团的“莱昂内尔”提出，或能用于囚禁一位叛变的铸之具名者。本书是对另一本更早、也更有争议的作品进行了大量修订后的版本。

readings.intro: The book was evidently revised some time after the Wars of the Roads had ended, but even then this kind of discussion would have been politically difficult.
readings.content: 'Lionel' suggests that the Disciplines of Scar and Hammer together would be necessary to create such a prison - but that either on its own would serve to release its occupant.

readings_cn.content: “莱昂内尔”暗示，要建造这样一座监狱，必须将伤疤与锤砧的戒律结合在一起——但单独使用其中任何一种都会释放它的囚犯。
readings_cn.intro: 本书显然是在路权战争结束后的一段时间里删改的，但即使如此，这种程度的讨论也足够引来政治上的麻烦。

tomes.name: The Carmine Petal: Unexpurgated
tomes.description: A project proposed by 'Lionel' of the Society of the Noble Endeavour by which, he claims, he succeeded in creating a sanctuary for a fugitive Forge-Name. The unexpurgated version.
tomes.description_cn: 一份由高贵之举社团的“莱昂内尔”提出的计划书，他声称自己已经成功为一位流亡的铸之具名者制造了避难所。本书为未经删节的版本。

readings.intro: At the time this book was written, a 'fugitive' Forge-Name would have been guilty of heresy, treason, or both.
readings.content: 'Lionel' suggests that the 'house of iron and fire' so created would include 'hollows of air and night', which would serve as a final hiding-place if the larger sanctuary were uncovered - though, he says, they could be easily revealed with invocations of the Disciplines either of Scar or of Hammer.

readings_cn.content: “莱昂内尔”表示，像这样创造出来的“铁与火之屋”将含有“气与夜的孔窍”，可在更大型的庇护所暴露后用作最后的藏身处——不过，他也说道，这种藏身处会在伤疤或锤砧的戒律下被轻松揭露。
readings_cn.intro: 在写下本书的时期，那位“流亡的”铸之具名者正被指控犯下了异端或叛国的罪名，或者兼而有之。

tomes.name: Letters To My Successor
tomes.description: Advice from Gervinus van Lauren, eleventh Librarian of Hush House, to the one who will come after him.
tomes.description_cn: 噤声居屋的第十一任图书管理员，格维努斯·范·劳伦给自己继任者的建议。

readings.intro: Some of the advice is practical - don't worry about losing the House Key; always close the seaward windows; make sure you feed the cockatoo. Much more of it is rarefied, specifically about the 'Inks of Revelation'. And some of it relates to van Lauren's own doom...
readings.content: 'When I was another, I made a foolish wager with the Hooded Princes, to solve seven riddles. I had not realised the riddles would be set by me for the one I would become. Six are resolved. The seventh will be the end of me. It waits now in the cellar of the Gaol, where Collers still believes I can keep it confined. But the first riddle told me I would not see the Second Dawn...'

readings_cn.content: “在我曾是另一个人时，和兜颈贵胄们打了个愚蠢的赌——解开七个谜题。我当时尚未意识到，这些谜题实际上将由我为自己将成为之人设下。如今，六者已了。第七个谜题将是我的结局。它就在监狱的地下室里等着我。科勒斯依然相信我能一直禁锢住它。但第一个谜题告诉我，我将不会见到第二拂晓……”
readings_cn.intro: 有些建议相当实用：不用担心自己会弄丢居屋的钥匙；永远不要打开向海一侧的窗户；记得喂鸡头鹦鹉。更多的则缥缈难解，尤其是关于“启示之墨”的那几条。有些则与范·劳伦自己的厄运有关……

tomes.name: From History to Eternity
tomes.description: A contraband manual of the Inks of Revelation. The author explains in a brief foreword that she is a high-ranking officer of 'an agency of the Duties' and that, though she supports its mission, she has concerns about the long-term consequences of its work.
tomes.description_cn: 一本遭禁的启示之墨介绍手册。作者在简短的前言之中自述是“某相关机构”的高层，虽然她认同该机构的使命，但却又对其工作的长远后果感到担忧。

readings.intro: 'All Histories braided into a golden loop; a shining ascent to Eternity. I had never imagined I could be afraid that there might be too few Truths. I could be wrong. But I'd like to leave at least one door ajar.'
readings.content: 'Ichor Auroral' can be brewed into an encaustum terminale associated with the Second History, using Inks of Revelation techniques with Rose aspect. The author warns that this is exceptionally difficult, since these techniques aren't aligned with Rose. 'But that's why I'm hoping the door will stay ajar, even once all the others are closed. I wish you luck.'

readings_cn.content: 使用“启示之墨”技艺和引相，便能将“曙光灵液”调制成第二史的终刻墨。作者也警告称，这种配方实现的难度是极高的，因为那些技术与引并不适配。“但这就是为什么我希望即使在其他门都闭合的情况下，那扇门仍能保持半开。祝你好运。”
readings_cn.intro: “所有的历史编成一个金色的圆环；一条通往永恒的耀眼路途。我从来不曾想象过自己可能因寥寥数条真理而恐惧。说不定我错了。但我想至少留下一扇半开的门。”

tomes.name: Nyn's Cages (Avignon Text)
tomes.description: The 'merciful measures' of the witch Nyn.
tomes.description_cn: 女巫宁记载的一些“仁慈的措施”。

readings.intro: Nyn's stated aim was to 'keep beyond the Walls of Sleep that business which should not trouble the world'. This includes fever, madness and delirium, as well as spirits identified as 'Devourers' and 'Deceivers'.
readings.content: Nyn warns against cutting hair, cracking mirrors, spilling blood, or invoking the Edicts Liminal or Inviolable before sleep - 'for no matter how secure a lock may be, its key will surely open it.'

readings_cn.intro: 宁公开宣称的目标是“将不该打扰世界之物阻挡在睡梦之墙外”。这包括发烧，疯狂与谵妄，同时还有被定义为“吞噬者”和“褪思者”的灵体。
readings_cn.content: 宁警告称，在睡前，不可剪下头发、打碎镜子、泼洒鲜血，或是唤起阈限或无侵之敕令——“因为不论锁有多么可靠，钥匙也一定能打开它。”

tomes.name: Nyn's Cages (Bruges Text, Illuminated)
tomes.description: The 'merciful measures' of the witch Nyn. This is only a partial version of the original, but it contains illustrations by Nyn's pupil, Mabelie of Bruges, which supplement the original.
tomes.description_cn: 女巫宁记载的一些“仁慈的措施”。本书只包含了原版的部分内容，但书中还附有宁的学徒，布鲁日的玛贝尔所绘制的插图，这为原版提供了补充。

readings.intro: Nyn's stated aim was to 'keep beyond the Walls of Sleep that business which should not trouble the world'. This includes fever, madness and delirium as well as spirits identified as 'Devourers' and 'Deceivers'. (Mabelie clearly enjoyed drawing both Devourers and Deceivers, but was less interested in illustrating disease symptoms.)
readings.content: Nyn warns against invoking the Edicts Liminal or Inviolable before sleep - 'for no matter how secure a lock may be, its key will surely open it.' Mabelie has helpfully illustrated this by drawing a sleepwalker clambering through an open window, about to leap into the jaws of a sea-monster. The sea-monster is goggle-eyed with happy anticipation.

readings_cn.intro: 宁公开宣称的目标是“将不该打扰世界之物阻挡在睡梦之墙外”。这包括发烧，疯狂与谵妄，同时还有被定义为“吞噬者”和“褪思者”的灵体。（显然，玛贝尔热衷于描绘吞噬者与褪思者，而对那些疾病的症状并不怎么感兴趣。）
readings_cn.content: 宁警告称，在睡前，不可唤起阈限或无侵之敕令——“因为不论锁有多么可靠，钥匙也一定能打开它。”玛贝尔的插画很好地说明了这一点：一位梦游者爬过敞开的窗户，马上就要跳进海怪的嘴里；而海怪则瞪大了眼睛，期待着送上门来的美味。

tomes.name: EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT
tomes.description: Ilse Bischoff's bewildering, widely derided final film.
tomes.description_cn: 伊尔莎·比绍夫的最后一部电影，令人困惑、广受嘲笑。

readings.intro: The film is an unrelenting fusillade of apparently unrelated images - birth, mirrors, grain-threshers, animal attacks, crowds at stations… but a single image appears again and again, dominating the rush of images until the film is only a single static shot.
readings.content: The repeating image is a view through a grimy window-pane of a nearby tower. There is a vague impression of flickering light around the tower-top. Just as the film ends, smoke plumes from the tower. That's it. Nothing of note at all… unless one happens to recognise the view of the Crucible Tower from the window of the Librarian's Quarters, and unless one happens to know that Ilse Bischoff never visited Brancrug, or even Britain, before her untimely death.

readings_cn.intro: 这部电影是由一系列看似毫不相关的画面组成的走马灯——出生、镜子、脱粒机、动物的袭击、车站的人群……但某幅图像一次又一次地出现，占据了越来越多的画面，直到电影最终变成了几乎静态的单一镜头。
readings_cn.content: 重复的图像是一幅透过肮脏的窗玻璃拍下的附近的塔的景象。塔顶周围隐约闪烁着灯光。影片临近尾声时，塔上冒出了滚滚浓烟。就是这样。没有什么值得注意的……除非某人碰巧认出那就是从图书管理员卧室窗户看到的坩埚塔，而且那人又碰巧知道伊尔莎·比绍夫在英年早逝之前从未去过布兰库格，甚至英国。

tomes.name: COLOURS IN THE LIVER
tomes.description: Ilse Bischoff's most controversial film, blamed for outbreaks of cannibalistic killings in Tiflis and Leipzig.
tomes.description_cn: 伊尔莎·比绍夫最具争议的作品。这部电影被认为引发了梯弗利斯和莱比锡的食人屠杀。

readings.intro: A gang of heretic priests agrees to strike the 'fear of the Change' into the infuriatingly atheist citizenry. At night they dress as four-winged angels and crawl down chimneys and through windows to savage members of their congregation.
readings.content: The priests are caught by unidentified figures wearing heavily mandibled masks, like grotesque caricatures of ants. They are force-fed larvae: a final caption indicates that at dawn the larvae will hatch…

readings_cn.intro: 一伙异端牧师决定将“对蜕变的恐惧”植入到恼人的无神论者市民心中。入夜，他们打扮成四翼天使，爬进烟囱、钻过窗户，袭击了他们的教众……
readings_cn.content: 牧师们被不明身份的人抓住了——他们戴着沉重的下颚面具，就像以漫画手法夸张了的怪诞蚂蚁。牧师们成了被强迫喂食的幼虫：最后的标题表明，拂晓时分，幼虫将孵化……

tomes.name: THE OPEN HEAD
tomes.description: Ilse Bischoff's hallucinatory quasi-documentary, notionally about the Greco-Turkish War of the previous decade.
tomes.description_cn: 伊尔莎·比绍夫的魔幻半纪录片，名义上讲的是前十年的希腊-土耳其战争。

readings.intro: A hammer-armed Turk and a sword-armed Greek pursue each other through the Pindus, setting traps for each other, robbing peasants, chalking insulting graffiti on walls. The tone is notionally anti-war, but any scholar of the invisible arts would recognise the Edge-hour subtext... and the Hyksos messages in the graffiti.
readings.content: The sword-wielder methodically fills a church with candles; lights each one; strips, again, to the waist to reveal his terrible scars; his chest somehow swings open like a cupboard door to reveal a blood-drenched book… and the film ends.

readings_cn.intro: 一个使锤的土耳其人和一个使剑的希腊人互相追逐着穿过品都斯山脉，彼此设置陷阱，抢劫农民，用粉笔在墙上涂画羞辱性的涂鸦。影片表面上的基调是反战的，但任何硏习无形之术的学者都能看出其中关于刃之司辰的潜台词……以及涂鸦中的希索克斯语信息。
readings_cn.content: 持剑者有条不紊地用蜡烛填满教堂，一支接一支地点亮，又将衣服褪至腰间，露出他那可怕的伤疤。他的胸膛如橱柜门一般转开，露岀一本鲜血淋漓的书……电影在此处戛然而止。

tomes.name: The Deaths of the Moon
tomes.description: A Haustorial tract on various forms of survival after death.
tomes.description_cn: 一篇吸器风格的短文，讨论了人在死后的各种存在形式。

readings.intro: When the heart no longer beats, the Grail may keep the spirit in the body, and an appetite is indicated to sustain. (Alukites are the best-known, but not the only, of this nature). This is the waning-moon mode…
readings.content: The full-moon mode is the intensification of one element of the soul to the point where ordinary sustension is unstable. Our Protector, the Generous of Hosts, began of this nature, and its generosity remains ungentle. It is possible for the body's health or the heart's chor to outpace the other elements, so that a static mode becomes impossible and growth proceeds in dramatic stages until balance remanifests...

readings_cn.intro: 当心脏不再跳动时，杯之准则可以将灵魂留在体内，并显现出一种食欲来维持存续。（吸血阿卢卡化是其中最广为人知的，但并非唯一具有这种性质的情况。）这就是残月态……
readings_cn.content: 满月态是一种魂质无法维持稳定时达到的活化状态。我们的守护者——“慷慨待客者”，就是从这种状态开始转变的，它的慷慨至今仍不温和。躯体的健康和心脏的脉律可能会超越其他魂质，因此保持静态是不可能的，且孳长会在一个戏剧性的阶段发生，直到平衡重新显现……

tomes.name: The Queen's Turn
tomes.description: A sixteenth-century translation of the Barrowchild's account of 'Lagiah's Turn' - when Lagiah, the Queen Unsated, was offered the opportunity to enter the service of the Hours of the Triple Knot, as long as she repudiated her brother-lover Antaios.
tomes.description_cn: 坟茔之子于十六世纪所著《拉吉亚的转变》的转译本——拉吉亚，无餍女王，只要她与自己的情人兼胞兄安泰俄斯断绝关系，就可以获得侍奉三重绳结会众司辰的机会。

readings.intro: Lagiah accepts, setting aside 'the arts of the low red sun' associated with Antaios. She bargains, however, for freedom for her daughters. The Hours of the Triple Knot accept casually, knowing that Lagiah has devoured her daughters - but wily Lagiah has decided, 'in the secret hollow of her heart', that she will adopt any who ask, if they can prove their fierceness.
readings.content: The traditions described here - the ones generally described as 'Hill and Hollow' - are associated with Lagiah before her Turn; but now that she's a Name of the Red Grail, they might also be safely used before an altar of the Triple Knot.

readings_cn.intro: 拉吉亚接受了条件，将与安泰俄斯有关的“低垂红日之技法”搁置一旁。然而她又以女儿们的自由为条件谈判。三重绳结会的诸司辰知道拉吉亚已经吞噬了她的女儿，便毫不在乎地接受了她的条件——但狡诈的拉吉亚已经“在她心中的秘密孔窍里”决定好，她会收养任何提出请求之人，只要她们能证明自己的残暴。
readings_cn.content: 文中描述的传统——现在称为“丘陵与孔窍”——与发生转变前的拉吉亚有关；但现在拉吉亚是赤杯的具名者，所以这些技艺也可以安全地在三重绳结会的祭坛前施展。

tomes.name: Skin of Silver
tomes.description: The epic of the final battle of the Lionsmith with the remnant-giant Antaios.
tomes.description_cn: 描绘了狮子匠与巨人孑遗安泰俄斯最后一战的史诗。

readings.intro: As always, the Lionsmith drew his strength from metal, and Antaios from stone… but the Lionsmith began to suspect also that this time, Antaios was drawing power from the Moon.
readings.content: The Lionsmith beseeches the Three for their assistance, and the Meniscate favours him with a skin of silver, like water, like mercury, so he too can drink power from the Moon; for, she whispers, he too will one day be drawn into a perfect balance.

readings_cn.content: 狮子匠向三者祈求帮助，而弧月赐予了他银质的皮肤，如水，如水银，如此他也能从月亮中汲取力量；因为，她轻语道，总有一天，他也会被引入完美的平衡之中。
readings_cn.intro: 和往常一样，狮子匠从金属中攫取力量，而安泰俄斯则是从岩石中……但狮子匠开始怀疑，安泰俄斯这次是在从月亮中攫取力量……

tomes.name: One Thousand Threads
tomes.description: The fate-supplications of the Matriarch of the Well, recorded in darkness by her weavers and her daughters…
tomes.description_cn: 井之女头领对命运的祈求，由她的织工与她的女儿在黑暗中记录下来……

readings.intro: The Well is long choked with rubble and ashes; the Matriarch long gone. She predicted her own end even as these supplications were recorded, but their power remains.
readings.content: Speak these supplications before an altar whose roots have drawn from a sacred spring; perhaps another root will rise towards daylight.

readings_cn.intro: 井早已被碎石和灰烬堵塞；女头领早已不在。早在这些祈求被记录之时，她就已经预言到了自己的结局，但其中的力量犹存。
readings_cn.content: 将这些祈求在一处植根于圣泉的祭坛前说出；也许另一条树根会向着日光升起。

tomes.name: The Carbonek Schism
tomes.description: The order of Obliviates, on the brink of schism, assembles in a Bounds-house identified only as 'Carbonek', after the Fisher-King's castle of legend. There the Know and the Long of the order debate their long policy of non-involvement in 'matters of Feather and Scale'.
tomes.description_cn: 名为忘却会的教团在濒临分裂之际，在一处仅知道名为“卡本内克”的边境建筑内举行了集会，此名典出自传说中渔夫王的城堡。教团内的通晓者与长生者就他们长久以来避免参与的“羽毛与鳞片”之问题进行了辩论。

readings.intro: One of their number - the one recording their debates - describes how in desperation he has found some kind of solution in a 'volume of transcendent heresy', but dares not pursue it alone. He convinces a handful of other Obliviates to depart Carbonek with him, while the others cross the sea to Port Noon.
readings.content: In the last few pages, the author reveals himself as the Know-adept Ambrose Westcott, writing in an uncharacteristically serious mode. He informs any who should find this work that he has returned the book he spoke of to 'Abbot Geffrey's Secret', where it can be retrieved with certain invocations of the Sacra Limiae. He hopes that one who has read this far, and understood this much, will find a History to determine.

readings_cn.content: 在最后的几页中，作者揭露了自己的身份：位列通晓者的学徒安布罗斯·威斯考特，此处他的文风一反常态地严肃。他告诉任何发现本书的人，他已经将自己在前文提到的那本书放回了被他称为“杰弗里院长的隐事”的地方，在那里使用“利米亚典仪”的某些祷文便可再次找回。他希望自己那位“阅读甚多、理解甚多”的继任者能找到一重历史来实现它。
readings_cn.intro: 其中的一员——也是这场辩论的记录者——描述了他是如何在绝望中于“一卷极度异端的典籍”中找到了某种解决方案，但不敢独自实践。他设法说服了少数同僚与他一同离开卡本内克，而其他人则横渡大海，前往午港。

tomes.name: The Wound-Wounds
tomes.description: 'A history of a hundred wars', sewn into a design of metallic threads that pursues itself across every page...
tomes.description_cn: “记述了一百场战争的历史”，其文字以金属丝线编织而成，在每一页上，丝线都如追逐般彼此缠绕着……

readings.intro: Darius and Alexander at Issus - the incandescent strivings of the Houses of Lancaster and York - the Second Worm War -
readings.content: The final page of the book depicts the first battles of a war among Hours, but the threads fray into alternatives, unbraiding from History. One of those threads is a coarse iron wire whose twists suggest the Disciplines of the Scar invoked before a subterranean configuration of iron, fire, and night...

readings_cn.intro: 大流士和亚历山大在伊苏斯的战争——兰开斯特家族和约克家族的炽热斗争——第二次蠕虫大战——
readings_cn.content: 本书的最后一页描写了司辰间的第一场纷争，可这些线却因磨损，呈现了与真正历史迥异的内容。其中的一根线是粗铁丝，它的缠绕暗示着要在钢铁，火焰和黑夜的地下祭坛前唤起“伤疤的戒律”……

tomes.name: Glimmerings
tomes.description: An anonymous prison diary written by a dreamer convicted of 'oneiric irresponsibility' and confined to the Cucurbit.
tomes.description_cn: 一本匿名的狱中日记，作者是一位梦者，因在梦中犯下“不负责任的愚行”而被收押在“炼金瓶”。

readings.intro: The prisoner is plainly terrified and bewildered by their situation, and has been unable to wrangle a coherent explanation out of anyone. But the dreams keep coming, and they keep writing them down…
readings.content: Snow; broken mirrors; half-heard sky music; flowers of white, red and black; a blood-streaked winter dawn... the most notorious signifiers of oneiric risk, fantastically vivid and detailed. No wonder they were locked up. Their final recorded dream is of a 'worm-jewel' beneath Brancrug Isle, which they open with a key carved from their finger-bone.

readings_cn.content: 雪；破碎的镜子；依稀可闻的天界之音；白色，红色与黑色的花；血痕道道的冬日拂晓……生动而详尽，无一不是代表梦境危害的最为声名狼藉的符号；难怪此人会被囚禁起来。最后被记录的梦境是布兰库格地下的“蠕虫珍宝”；此人用自己指骨雕刻的钥匙打开了它。
readings_cn.intro: 囚犯显然对自己的处境感到恐惧与困惑，而且无法从任何人那里得到合乎逻辑的解释。但是，梦境不断出现，于是此人继续将它们记录在纸上……

tomes.name: The Wonderful Shape
tomes.description: Blessings and invocations of the Triple Knot recorded at a sanctuary in Cyprus notable for its weavers, sculptors, and gardeners.
tomes.description_cn: 三重绳结会的祝福与祷文，于塞浦路斯的一所以纺织、雕塑与园艺闻名的圣殿内记录。

readings.intro: 'The roots go deep. The knots remain…'
readings.content: The final invocation is one for the 'Restoration of the Roots', to be spoken before an altar of the Triple Knot - but, puzzlingly, it should not be spoken by any priestess of the Knot, or even by one who has been initiated into their Mysteries.

readings_cn.intro: “根往深繁。绳结长存……”
readings_cn.content: 最后的祷文是献给“根之恢复”的，可在三重绳结会的祭坛前说出——但令人费解的是，这个祷文不应由姐妹会内的神职人员说出，甚至连那些参与过她们仪式的人也不行。

tomes.name: The Grand Passage of the Hours
tomes.description: The Limian Burzghash's gazetteer of the patterns and rhythms of the Hours' progress through the Mansus, from Concursum to Malleary, Malleary to Wood…
tomes.description_cn: 利米亚教团成员布兹加什编撰的地名辞典，记录了诸司辰在漫宿中行进的章法与节律，从聚点到锤炼场，从锤炼场到林地……

readings.intro: 'Each century in the Mansus is a great feasting-hall. In each ninety-ninth year, the hall falls silent; the Elegiast sits alone at the feast.'
readings.content: 'There are paths in the Mansus that only the Sun has walked. In the time of the Sun's Division, who will know them? When the Second Dawn comes, who will walk them?'

readings_cn.content: “有些道途只有太阳曾走过。在太阳遭分裂之时，有谁将知晓？当第二拂晓到来时，有谁将踏足？”
readings_cn.intro: “每个世纪在漫宿都是一楹新的宴厅。到了第九十九个年头，厅堂会陷入沉寂；而悼歌诗人独坐宴席。”

tomes.name: The Messenger Awaiting Her Destination
tomes.description: The Limian Burzghash records his prophecies of a City Unbuilt, and entreaties to its Herald.
tomes.description_cn: 利米亚教团成员布兹加什对某座未建之城预言的记录，也包含了对其使节的恳求。

readings.intro: 'The Herald may never arrive at the City Unbuilt. The City may never be built without the Herald's Message…'
readings.content: The Herald is finally identified as the 'Twelfth Initiate of the House of Silence'. The foundation-stone will be taken from the House of Silence, Burzghash suggests, to become the foundation-stone of the City Unbuilt…

readings_cn.content: 使节最终被认定是“沉默居屋的第十二位新晋者”。布兹加什提议说，未建之城的基石应取自沉默居屋的基石……
readings_cn.intro: “使节恐怕永远无法到达未建之城。可没有使节的来访，城市恐怕永远无法建起……”

tomes.name: The Road to Janus
tomes.description: The Limian Burzghash makes a series of prophecies regarding 'the Initiates of the House of Silence', with intricate, if unhelpful, predictions on their passage through the House.
tomes.description_cn: 利米亚教团成员布兹加什对“沉默居屋的新晋者们”做出的一系列预言。他对他们去往居屋的旅程进行了晦涩难懂而毫无帮助的预测。

readings.intro: 'The Sixth Initiate is Priest and Key, Gate and Church. He shall cross the sea and open the tide. He shall not be the Eleventh, yet shall there be Seven between them. In the first Year of his Time, the Flower-Door is opened…'
readings.content: 'The Twelfth Initiate is Salvation and Wrack, Steed and Rider, who chooseth one Blossom of Three, who casteth away the Key and whom the Key shall not cast away, who comes after the Flame and before the Snow….'

readings_cn.content: “第十二位新晋者是救赎与海难，骏马与骑手；此人选择三花的其中一朵；此人抛弃钥匙，钥匙却不会弃主而去；此人自烈火之后，冰雪之前到来……”
readings_cn.intro: “第六位新晋者是教士与钥匙，门扉与教堂。他将跨越大海，分开浪潮。他不会是第十一位，然他们会同享七者。他到来的第一年，花之门被开启……”

tomes.name: Green Jasper Tablet
tomes.description: Supposedly copied from a tablet of green jasper which serves as the Covenant-stone of the Monastery of the Fifth Cup - the token which gives that Library shelter beneath the Watchman's Tree.
tomes.description_cn: 据传，本书是从一块碧玉石板上誊抄来的。那块石板是第五杯修道院的盟约石——是图书馆在守夜人之树下受到庇护的象征。

readings.intro: 'Humankind hid itself from the Glory's light in the Roots of the Watchman's Tree. But for every chink we stuffed with cloth and hair, we opened another, and the light crept in. Until we looked below, into Nowhere, and the Eye of the Mare-in-the-Tree winked Red...'
readings.content: The Tablet expounds the dangers of inviting in the Nowhere-Hour called the Mare-in-the-Tree, and also of forbidding her entry, since she can never entirely be denied. Along the way, it reveals the secret of the Sacrament Malachite ('in which the merry Mare merrily spits') - brewed with the Rites of the Roots from the numa-pear, in the presence of sufficient Nectar-aspect.

readings_cn.intro: “人类藏身于守夜人之树的根部以躲避辉光的光芒，可每当我们用布条和头发堵住一个缝隙，就会打开另一个缝隙，光便悄然照了进来。直到我们望向下方，深入虚界，树中牝马的眸子红光闪闪……”
readings_cn.content: 碑文阐述了邀请被称为树中牝马的虚界司辰的危险性，也阐述了禁止她进入的危险性，因为她永远不会被完全拒绝。同时，碑文还揭示了孔雀石圣餐的秘密（“愉悦的牝马欢快地把口水吐入其中”）——可在有足够蜜相的情况下，用闰时之梨以“根系之仪”调制而成。

tomes.name: White Jade Tablet
tomes.description: Supposedly copied from a tablet of white jade which serves as the Covenant-stone of the Grove of the Green Immortals - the token which gives that Library shelter beneath the Watchman's Tree.
tomes.description_cn: 据传，本书是从一块白玉石板上誊抄来的。那块石板是翠仙苑的盟约石——是图书馆在守夜人之树下受到庇护的象征。

readings.intro: 'When humankind emerged from the weft of the Roots, we were smeared with the filth of crumbled ages. The foolish sought to wash it from themselves, but our skins were yet soft, and fell easily from us…'
readings.content: The Tablet expounds the dangers (and pleasures) of abandoning appearances in search of essence. Along the way, it reveals the secret of Skinshuck Mead, which can be brewed from honey by application of the Rites of the Roots, if enough Moth-aspect is present.

readings_cn.content: 碑文阐述了舍弃表象而追求内里的危险性（及乐趣）。同时，它也揭示了剥皮蜜酒的秘密——可用蜂蜜在有足够蛾相的情况下，以“根系之仪”调制而成。
readings_cn.intro: “当人类从根系的纬丝中诞生时，我们的身上沾满破碎年代的污垢。愚者试图洗净身上的污垢，可那时我们的皮肤还很柔嫩，极易从身上脱落……”

tomes.name: Xenodicene Odes
tomes.description: Poetry attributed to Xenodice, Name of the Horned-Axe.
tomes.description_cn: 献给刻赛诺狄刻——双角斧的具名者的诗歌。

readings.intro: In the House of Lethe's heyday, it held an annual competition where its initiates competed to produce the best ode in Xenodice's honour. So there are still a lot of odes out there.
readings.content: It has never been clear why the Letheans, who avoided traffic with the Hours with the occasional exception of the Elegiast, would devote effort to a Name of the Horned-Axe. Perhaps Xenodice was just a suitably challenging subject…

readings_cn.content: 人们一直都难以理解，除了偶尔与悼歌诗人来往，总是避免与诸司辰打交道的遗忘家族，为什么会费心歌颂双角斧的具名者。可能只是因为刻赛诺狄刻这个主题很适合当做挑战项目而已……
readings_cn.intro: 在遗忘家族的鼎盛时期，每年都会举办一场比赛，让它的新晋者们竞相创作最好的颂歌来赞美刻赛诺狄刻。正因如此，现在仍有许多颂歌流传于世。

tomes.name: Quirinic Meditations
tomes.description: Battle-apothegms of the Name Quirinus.
tomes.description_cn: 具名者奎里努斯的战斗箴言集。

readings.intro: Quirinus of the Two-Headed Spear is one of the more approachable Names of the Colonel - still grave and inflexible, but more inclined to divulge occasionally useful advice…
readings.content: When Quirinus was honoured in Rome, he was sometimes associated with the enigmatic god Janus - especially in the rites of the Unnumbered Legion. The advice in these pages doesn't confirm any such connection, but does suggest a more philosophical side to this warrior-Name.

readings_cn.content: 奎里努斯在罗马受到崇敬时，人们有时会将其与神秘莫测的雅努斯神联系在一起，尤其是在无尽军团的仪式中。书中的建议并不能证明存在过类似的联系，但确实展示了这位身为战士的具名者更富哲学性的一面。
readings_cn.intro: “双头矛”奎里努斯是上校的具名者中较为平易近人的一位——尽管仍然严肃且顽固，但他偶尔也愿意透露一些实用建议……

tomes.name: Medusan Commentaries
tomes.description: Haustorial discussions of Medusa's histories.
tomes.description_cn: 吸器关于美杜莎之历史的论述集。

readings.intro: 'Medusa's Riddle: 'What Is Not Seen?' She might be the oldest of her kind still living; and she is dead. Once she held the key to the door in the Wood; and though perhaps she lost it, she holds it still…
readings.content: The scholars of the Haustorium seem to suggest that just as there are always seven Ligeians but they are not always the same, there is always one Medusa but she is not always the same. There does seem to be more of a common thread of identity than simply a series of titled successors, and here the Haustorium's argument becomes harder to follow - especially because the Haustorium and its members themselves have an unusual concept of individual identity...

readings_cn.intro: “美杜莎的谜语是：‘何物不得见？’她可能是她这类当中还活着的最年迈的一位，不过她已经死了。她曾持有通往林地中那扇门的钥匙；虽然她可能失去了这把钥匙，可她仍然持有它……”
readings_cn.content: 吸器的学者们认为，正如总有七位丽姬亚，但不总是那七位一样，美杜莎也总有一位，但并不总是那一位。除了同是一个头衔的继任者外，她们的身份似乎还有更多的共同之处。吸器的观点在这里变得令人费解——尤其是因为吸器和它的成员本身在个体身份认同的观念上就异于常人……

results.result_name_cn: 教诲：覆画残迹与古老前身

tomes.name: Echidnalia
tomes.description: Part genealogy, part taxonomy, part family gossip - a closely detailed, highly specialised account of one branch of the complex brood of children associated with the Ligeian Echidna.
tomes.description_cn: 这本书既是家谱，也是分类学研究，还是家族八卦——它详尽而专业地介绍了丽姬亚厄客德娜复杂子代中的一个分支。

readings.intro: The gods-who-were-Stone knew the uses of the Biting Key, and now Echidna claims it. She has birthed so many children, and some yet survive.
readings.content: Echidna's children are of two kinds: 'born' and 'won'. She seems to have had some success in winning over the creations of other powers to her service. In particular she has a habit of giving sustenance to the labhites, who consume what is found in the sky, and seducing them away from the Lionsmith...

readings_cn.intro: 过去石源神们知晓咬噬之钥的用途，而现在厄客德娜持有它。她生育了许许多多的子嗣，其中有些幸存至今。
readings_cn.content: 厄客德娜的子嗣分为两类：“生下的”和“赢得的”。她似乎许多次成功赢得了其他神灵造物的侍奉。她尤其乐于投喂只吃天空中食物的狻猊，并引诱它们叛离狮子匠……

tomes.name: Naenian Sketches
tomes.description: Travelogues and studies exchanged by raggies and ghouls - that is, the Long who've ascended under the patronage of the Sun-in-Rags and those who won the attention of the Elegiast.
tomes.description_cn: 残破者们与食尸鬼们交流的游记和习作——二者分别指在残阳的庇佑下飞升的长生者，以及赢得悼歌诗人关注的长生者。

readings.intro: 'Naenia is the Elegiast's Name, but she has always stood high in the Sun-in-Rags' favour; and she offers her consolations also to those Long who have taken him as a patron...'
readings.content: Both kinds of Winter-long know that their death is only deferred, so both tend to seek and treasure beauty. Here they detail their purest experiences - the mountain after the avalanche, the peace after the storm-wreck, the gusted silence of the sun-shadowed hill...

readings_cn.intro: “挽歌儿是悼歌诗人的具名者，但她同时也深受残阳的宠爱；所以她也宽慰那些视残阳为庇护者的长生者。”
readings_cn.content: 冬之长生者都知道，他们的死亡只是被推迟了而已，所以都倾向于追求和珍惜美。本书中他们详细地描述了自己最纯粹的经历——雪崩后的山峦，风暴肆虐后的宁静，日光阴影下徒然寂静的山丘……

tomes.name: Plantagenet Mysteries
tomes.description: Exhaustive attempts to analyse and renew the Blood of the Sun by one of the numerous occult societies, after the manner of the Endeavour Club, for whatever squalid political motive.
tomes.description_cn: 众多的神秘社团中的一个，出于某种卑劣的政治动机，仿效高贵之举社团的方式，对太阳的血脉进行了详尽的分析和补充。

readings.intro: '…until the King fell beneath his great Steed in its Utmost Configuration. By the time he could be cut free, his Alloy had already begun to tarnish, and that Day was ever afterwards known as his Great Misfortune…'
readings.content: 'Since the Sun and the Forge had both bestowed their Favour, one could not remove it without the other - or would not. But neither could the Alloy be renewed by any Power in the Mansus. So the King looked beyond the Mansus - beyond the Bounds…'

readings_cn.content: “既然骄阳与铸炉共同给予了祂们的恩惠，任何一位便无法（或是不会）在没有另一位的情况下单独收回其恩惠。但因此也没有任何漫宿的神灵能修复受损的合金。所以国王将目光投向了漫宿之外——边境之外……”
readings_cn.intro: “……直到国王从高头大马的背上摔下，并被那匹功率全开的马压在身下。当他被解救出来时，他的合金已然开始褪色，那一天自此被称为他的‘大不幸’……”

tomes.name: Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903
tomes.description: A confidential journal kept by Greene, former Nocturnal Branch Superindent but, by 1903, Librarian of the House. Greene has kept his journal in Hyksos, presumably as an extra measure of privacy.
tomes.description_cn: 格林写的一本机密日志，他曾是夜勤处的警司，并于1903年就任居屋的图书管理员一职。格林用希克索斯语写了这本日志，大概是为了极端地保护他的隐私。

readings.intro:
In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'
readings.content:
The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau... 

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.

readings_cn.intro:
1903年，居屋和夜勤处合作密切，而格林则是这场合作明面上的代言人。然而，显然格林私底下对夜勤处失望至极，他愈发认为其没有履行好职责。他对建造在布兰库格监狱下方的“镇压装置”尤为担忧。
“司辰和具名者都很危险，”他写道，“但至少我们应对祂们的措施都建立在长期的经验之上。但这样一位司辰：行动早于诞生之神——自从未进入之处离去之神——如果她的具名者行于世间，我们要如何才能了解祂们的能力与行动方式？”
readings_cn.content: 交替出现的算式（潮汐，日期，财务测算）和对“A·F”的热望的表述组成了日志最后的记录。格林似乎打算带着A·F远走高飞，其中有些算式表明，他一直以来都在挪用资金，奥尔图基奥事件及随后夜勤处重组为防剿局时的混乱局面为其提供了掩护……然而，这些记录在这年结束前便戛然而止。格林是否真的带着这些资金与挚友潜逃，以及他是否出于其他原因丢弃了这本日志，均不明了。

journals.name: A Drowned Book
journals.description: The one possession I kept from the shipwreck. It must be important to me. [The Aspects below tell you more about how and where you can use this item. Hover over them to learn more.]
journals.description_cn: 我从海难之中唯一保留下来的财产，这对我来说一定很重要。[下方的性相会告诉你如何使用该物品，以及在哪里使用该物品，鼠标悬停以显示详细内容。]

journals.name: Gunmetal Book
journals.description: The heavy metal cover nearly took me down with it. But I survived, and so will this.
journals.description_cn: 沉重的金属封面几乎使我与之一同沉没。而我活下来了，它将也一样。

journals.name: Mottled Book
journals.description: The cover is unusual. Horn? Bakelite? Chitin? I should be able to remember.
journals.description_cn: 这封面不同寻常。角？胶木？几丁质？我应该能记起来。

journals.name: Scarred Book
journals.description: Goatskin? Antelope? Some scarred leather that catches at my memory. I should know.
journals.description_cn: 山羊皮？羚羊皮？伤痕累累的皮革勾起了我的回忆。我应该知道的。

journals.name: Scaled Book
journals.description: The scaled binding has survived the soaking well enough.
journals.description_cn: 覆盖着鳞片的封面在浸泡之后保存良好。

journals.name: Coppery Book
journals.description: The unusual metal binding is untouched by the sea.
journals.description_cn: 不同寻常的金属封面并未被大海损伤。

journals.name: Stone-Studded Book
journals.description: Dull-gleaming yellowish stones. Amber? I feel that I should know...
journals.description_cn: 淡黄色的发微光石。琥珀？我觉得我应该知道……

journals.name: Silvery Book
journals.description: Is that real silver? I feel that it should be. I should remember.
journals.description_cn: 那真的是银质的吗？我感觉它理当是。我理当记得。

journals.name: Feathered Book
journals.description: The feathers that adorn its cover are bedraggled from its time in the sea.
journals.description_cn: 装饰封面的羽毛因浸泡在海中而湿透了。

journals.name: Silken Book
journals.description: The binding is unusual - and half-familiar - some kind of silk? It's survived its soaking remarkably well.
journals.description_cn: 这封面不寻常——却有些熟悉——某种丝绸？它在浸泡中保存得很好。

journals.name: Ironclad Journal
journals.description: I have striven to be the last Librarian of Hush House. This journal records my strivings. You might wish to begin your studies with the Horomachistry Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我一直在争取成为噤声居屋的最后一任图书管理员，这本日记记录了我的抗争之路。[革命者最深切的愿望就是，来到噤声居屋，以开辟一重推翻最底层律法的崭新历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从司辰学智慧开始你的研究。]

[The Executioner's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a new History which will atone for their crimes; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Preservation Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我让许多怪奇之物安息。我曾认为这是正确的。如今我却为犯下错事而忧虑。我是噤声居屋的图书管理员，在这里，我会确保他们将被铭记。[处刑者最深切的愿望就是，来到噤声居屋，以记录一重偿赎罪孽的崭新历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从保存术智慧开始你的研究。]

journals.name: Sand-Scarred Journal
journals.description: I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will record what arose from my Crime and my Curse. [The Archaeologist's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a History where their crime could be forgiven... or redefined. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Skolekosophy Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我是噤声居屋的图书管理员，而这本日记将记录我的罪恶与诅咒曾招致何祸。[考古学家最深切的愿望就是，来到噤声居屋，以记录下一重其罪孽能被偿清、抑或被重新定义的历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从蠕虫学智慧开始研究。]

journals.name: Serpentskin Journal
journals.description: I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will be my Perpetual Map. [The Cartographer's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to chart a new History in which their impossible map would be possible; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Nyctodromy Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我是噤声居屋的图书管理员，且在这里，我将绘成我的无尽地图。[制图师最深切的愿望就是，来到噤声居屋，以绘制一重使其那不可能的地图变为可能的历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从夜游术智慧开始你的研究。]

journals.name: Hammered Copper Journal
journals.description: I've crossed three oceans and almost drowned in one. Now I am the Librarian of Hush House. Perhaps here I will be safe from my parents; but I can't take that for granted. [The Prodigal's dearest wish is sanctuary - as Librarian, or in a History where things are different;but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Ithastry Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我曾跨越三片海洋，还差点溺死在其中一片，如今我是噤声居屋的图书管理员。此处或可保我免遭父母所害；但也不能觉得这就理所当然。[浪子最深切的愿望就是寻到庇护——成为一名图书管理员，抑或是去往一重情况有所不同的历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从盗火术智慧开始你的研究。]

journals.name: Amber-Flecked Journal
journals.description: I am the Twice-Born Librarian of Hush House, and this is the journal in which I keep my remaining memories. [The Twiceborn's 'third choice' might be life as the Librarian, or it might be something more radical. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Illumination Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我二度降生于世，现在是噤声居屋的图书管理员。这是一本记录了我残存回忆的日记。[二度降生者的“第三个选择”可能是作为一名图书管理员度过余生……也可能更加激进。但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从照明术智慧开始你的研究。]

journals.name: Silver-Bound Journal
journals.description: I was rich; but something was missing. I am no longer rich... and still, something is missing. Hush House is a place of conclusions, and here, as Librarian, I may find mine. [The Magnate came to the House to conclude a History where they will find peace; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Hushery Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: 我曾富有，但缺失了什么。我不再富有……但仍缺失了什么。噤声居屋是一个终末之地。在此处，作为一位图书管理员，我或许可以找回我的那样东西。[富豪来到噤声居屋，期以得终于一重能寻得安宁的历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从静默术智慧开始研究。]

journals.name: Feather-Decked Journal
journals.description: In Caer Adar I heard the secret gods speak one to another. I thought that would be the end of my journey, but the more I heard, the more I knew must be missing. I am the Librarian of Hush House, and I will find what has been lost. [The Symurgist came to Hush House to find a History with the songs that have fallen to silence; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Birdsong Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: “在凯尔·亚达，我听到了隐秘诸神间相互分享的秘密。我以为那些秘密会是我旅途的结尾，但我听得越多，必须忘却的就越多。我是噤声居屋的图书管理员，我会寻到我之所失。”[鸟慧者来到噤声居屋，期以寻找一重保存着已然沉寂之歌的历史；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从鸟鸣学智慧开始研究。]

journals.name: Bee-Silk Journal
journals.description: 'Picasso? I'll give you Picasso.' [The Artist came to Hush House to shape and share a History of primal, ultimate, unprecedented experience; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Bosk Wisdom.]
journals.description_cn: “毕加索？那我就给你看看毕加索。”[艺术家来到噤声居屋，期以塑造与分享一种既原始又终极的空前体验；但你可以通过记录任何一重历史来完成游戏。你可能会希望从丛林学智慧开始研究。]

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Dog
aspecteditems.description: A bottomless and reproachful appetite! But such a good bottomless appetite!
aspecteditems.description_cn: 无底而可耻的胃口！可又是如此好的胃口！

aspecteditems.description: Walkies are surely a small price to pay for his unshakeable fidelity.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 散步对换取他那不渝的忠贞而言无疑只是小小的代价。

aspecteditems.name: Stray Dog
aspecteditems.description: Lost, frightened, eager.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 茫然，恐惧，饥肠辘辘。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Gull
aspecteditems.description: Squawking urgently.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 急切地鸣叫。

aspecteditems.description: As noisy and demanding as it was in its youth. But much bigger.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 和它还是雏鸟时一样吵闹且挑剔。但体型要大得多。

aspecteditems.description: A peeping little thing, its mother is dead or flown.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一只唧唧叫的小家伙，它的妈妈不是死了就是飞走了。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Relic
aspecteditems.description: Quarrelsome, until it feeds again.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 直到再次被喂食前，它都在吵闹。

aspecteditems.name: Living Relic

aspecteditems.description_cn: 在这个太阳照耀的世界里鲜能见到这种存在。

aspecteditems.name: Savage Relic
aspecteditems.description: A shrieking little bundle of primordial ill-temper.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一小团尖叫着的、自远古而来的暴脾气。

aspecteditems.name: Stymphling
aspecteditems.description: Eva Dewulf taught her father Valentine how to hatch these silvery little villains, but he never learnt to like them.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 伊娃·德沃尔夫教会了她的父亲瓦伦丁如何孵化这些银色的小坏蛋，但他从没学会喜欢上它们。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Stymphling
aspecteditems.name_cn: 饥饿的斯廷法利斯湖兽
aspecteditems.description: Hissing avidly.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 急切的嘶嘶声。

aspecteditems.name: Unimpressed Cat
aspecteditems.description: RECENTLY THERE HAS BEEN A DEARTH OF FOOD. YOU WILL UNDERSTAND THE GRAVITY OF THE SITUATION. NO DOUBT YOU ARE EAGER TO RECTIFY IT.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 近日食物短缺。你会明白形势有多严峻。毫无疑问，你也急于改正。

aspecteditems.name: Pet Cat
aspecteditems.description: Oh? Were you hoping to work on that desk?
aspecteditems.description_cn: 哦？你想在那张桌子上工作吗？

aspecteditems.name: Stray Cat
aspecteditems.description: Feed some animals and earn their loyalty. Feed this one, and earn its patience.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 喂养其他动物能获得它们的忠诚。但喂养这只，获得的是它的耐心。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Viper
aspecteditems.description: Inclined to strike, although sluggishly, until fed.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 相当慵懒，可仍有攻击倾向——直到被喂饱。

aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位对暖壁炉，温老鼠与热牛奶如饥似渴的研究者。

aspecteditems.name: Wild Viper
aspecteditems.description: Don't make any sudden moves.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 不要做任何突然的举动。

aspecteditems.description: Was this magnificent and indomitable beast named for the rector's indomitable and magnificent housekeeper? Best not to inquire too closely.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这只高贵且倔犟的鸟禽是得名自教区牧师家那位倔犟且高贵的女管家吗？还是别打听太多为妙。

aspecteditems.name: Resentful Terrence
aspecteditems.description: Cluck. CLUCK.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 咯咯，咯咯。

aspecteditems.description_cn: 所有见到她的人都会同意，土便士最显著的特征，便是她并非特伦士。

aspecteditems.name: Pleading Tuppence
aspecteditems.description: Cluck. …cluck?
aspecteditems.description_cn: 咯咯……咯咯？

aspecteditems.name: Magnificent Green Cockatoo
aspecteditems.description: On numerous occasions, this wonderful bird has remained almost entirely inaudible.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这种不可思议的鸟儿在很多地区都难觅踪迹。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Green Cockatoo
aspecteditems.description: On numerous occasions, this wonderful bird has remained almost entirely inaudible.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这种不可思议的鸟儿在很多地区都难觅踪迹。

aspecteditems.name: Hungry Imago
aspecteditems.description: Torpid with hunger.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 因饥饿而蛰伏。

aspecteditems.description: It's come so far. Release it, and it could fly farther.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 它已经远达至此。放生它，它就能飞得更远。

aspecteditems.description: Approaching the chrysalis crossroads.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 接近化蛹的十字路口。

aspecteditems.name: Solomon's Preparation
aspecteditems.description: Solomon Husher would take this every night without fail before sleep, to close his ears to the sound of the waves. But on the 9th of January 1838, a heavy snow fell on Hush House. When the other residents dug themselves out, Husher was nowhere to be found. He had left a resignation letter, and an undrunk measure of his Preparation.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 所罗门·赫舍每夜入眠前都会喝下这种东西，以免听见海潮之声，从无例外。但在1838年1月9日，一场大雪覆盖了噤声居屋。当其他住户把自己刨出来时，赫舍却了无踪迹。他留下了一封辞呈，以及一整罐未曾饮用的这种制剂。

aspecteditems.description: The Ravelines abandoned their lands, and yet, someone is still making this wine.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 拉维林家族抛弃了他们的土地，但仍有人在生产这种葡萄酒。

aspecteditems.name: Canvas
aspecteditems.description: (YOUR PICTURE HERE)
aspecteditems.description_cn: （上面是你的肖像）

aspecteditems.name: Hallowed Anthropoderm
aspecteditems.description: Yes, it's human skin, but it's not just human skin.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 没错，这是人类的皮肤，但它可不只是人类的皮肤。

aspecteditems.name: Nivine Parchment
aspecteditems.description: Pale as the first wisp of mountain-cloud.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 苍白如山峦的第一缕云冠。

aspecteditems.name: Quire of Paper
aspecteditems.description: Creamy-smooth, eagerly awaiting ink.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 奶油般顺滑，渴盼着墨水。

aspecteditems.name: 'Ambrose Westcott'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is cast in brass.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用黄铜铸造的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Brian Levinsen'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is cast from aluminium - oxidised to grey.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是铝质的——已经氧化变灰。

aspecteditems.name: 'Sir David Greene'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is carved from reddish granite.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用浅红花岗岩雕成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Eva Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: This is the crystal called scolecite - the worm-stone - polished to chill smoothness.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是由名为钙沸石——又称蠕虫石的水晶雕刻的，被打磨至泛出寒光。

aspecteditems.name: 'Fraser Strathcoyne'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is shaped from beeswax. Careful with it!
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用蜂蜡雕成的。小心磕碰！

aspecteditems.name: 'Gervinus van Lauren'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is cast in highly polished bronze.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是由高度抛光的青铜铸成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Gideon Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: The bust is terracotta, brightly painted.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像由陶瓷制成，漆色鲜艳。

aspecteditems.name: 'Hendrik Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: Hendrik Dewulf, 1st Baron Brancrug, known for his pious, merciless justice. Granted Brancrug Isle in 1536 after the dissolution of St Brandan's.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 亨德里克·德沃尔夫，第一代布兰库格男爵，以虔诚与无情的正义而闻名。圣布伦丹修道院被解散后，他于1536年受赐成为了布兰库格岛的所有者。

aspecteditems.name: 'Kitty Mazarine'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is carved from black limestone.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用黑色大理石雕刻成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Musgrave Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: The bust is carved from wood - cherry?
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用木头雕刻成的——樱桃木？

aspecteditems.name: 'Natalia Brulleau'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is cast in iron.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是以铁铸造的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Serena Blackwood'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is carved from alabaster.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用雪花石膏雕成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Solomon Husher'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is the palest white marble.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用淡白至极的大理石雕成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Thirza Blake'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is carved from malachite.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用孔雀石雕成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Thomas Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: The bust is carved from limestone.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是用石灰岩雕成的。

aspecteditems.name: 'Valentine Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: Valentine Dewulf, 6th Baron Brancrug, known for his eccentricities. 'IN THE SKY HE SOUGHT HIS FRIENDS', an inscription reads.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 瓦伦丁·德沃尔夫，第六代布兰库格男爵，以他的种种怪癖为所人知。“他在天空中找到了朋友”，雕像上的铭文这么写着。

aspecteditems.name: 'Walter Dewulf'
aspecteditems.description: The bust is carved from serpentinite - a striking local stone.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是由蛇纹石雕成——一种引人注目的本地石材。

aspecteditems.name: 'Willem Harries'
aspecteditems.description: This bust is cast in highly polished bronze.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 这座半身像是由高度抛光的青铜铸成的。

aspecteditems.name: Abandoned Luggage
aspecteditems.description: Long past the help of any lost-and-found.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 早就超出了任何失物招领规定的时限。

aspecteditems.name: Box of Oddities
aspecteditems.description: A tiny treasury of forgotten things. Perhaps there's a real oddity in here somewhere.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一个装着被遗忘之物的小小宝库。没准里边某处藏有真正的奇物。

aspecteditems.name: Box of Rarities
aspecteditems.description: A tiny treasury of forgotten things. Perhaps there's a real rarity in here somewhere.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一个装着被遗忘之物的小小宝库。没准里边某处藏有真正的珍品。

aspecteditems.name: Records Box
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by a musician-spy.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位音乐家兼密探存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Attaché Case
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by a diplomat-folklorist.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位外交官兼民俗学家存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Ambered Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by an adept on the cusp of ascension to Lantern-long.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位即将晋升为灯之长生者的学徒所存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Coppery Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by the doomed child of two immortals, seeking sanctuary at Hush House from the terrible hunger of their parents.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 两名不朽者那注定毁灭的子嗣所储存的珍宝，此人曾为躲避双亲那骇人的饥饿而来到噤声居屋寻求庇护。

aspecteditems.name: Hive Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by a visionary apiarist with Blomberende lineage.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位富有远见且有绽莓血统的养蜂人所存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Imperial Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by an exiled empress.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位被流放的皇后存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Ironclad Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by an esoteric anarch on the eve of her failed revolution.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位修习秘术的无政府主义者在她那注定失败的革命前夕存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Morbid Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure bequeathed by a death-haunted merchant-prince in his last days.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位饱受死亡纠缠的商界巨头在他最后的日子里遗赠的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Mottled Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure donated by a disgraced Tragularius assassin.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位声名狼藉的图拉古拉里刺客捐赠的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Royal Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by a king before his final sacrifice.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位国王于他做出最终的牺牲前存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Scaled Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure left behind by an explorer on the eve of his final voyage.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一位探险家在他最后一次航行前夕留下的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Scarred Casket
aspecteditems.description: A treasure stored by an accursed tomb-robber - or something that walked in her shape.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一名被诅咒的盗墓者——亦或是以她的形体行走于世之物所存储的珍宝。

aspecteditems.name: Souvenir Cache
aspecteditems.description: Memories tidily tucked away until now.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 回忆在其中整整齐齐地储藏至今。

aspecteditems.name: Contraband Flotsam
aspecteditems.description: Salt-stained and wave-wracked.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 饱受风浪摧残，表面满是盐渍。

aspecteditems.name: Contraband Jetsam
aspecteditems.description: Flung overboard in furtive haste.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 被匆忙地偷偷丢进海里。

aspecteditems.name: Crate of Supplies
aspecteditems.description: Something set helpfully aside.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 遭到遗弃的有用物资。

aspecteditems.name: Abandoned Packages
aspecteditems.description: Battered but unbreached.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 老旧，但完好。

aspecteditems.name: Forsaken Packages
aspecteditems.description: They plead mutely to be opened. No-one else ever cared to.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 它们无声地请求人们打开。可从没人留意过。

aspecteditems.name: Lost Packages
aspecteditems.description: The label is smeared to unreadable fog.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 上面的标签被污渍遮盖，无法辨认。

aspecteditems.name: Slim Parcel
aspecteditems.description: Carefully wrapped in brown paper.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 用牛皮纸精心包装。

aspecteditems.name: Tall Parcel
aspecteditems.description: Tightly wrapped in oilcloth.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 紧紧地包着一层油布纸。

aspecteditems.name: Investigator's Suitcase
aspecteditems.description: A suitcase that once belonged to someone in the habit of shining a light in dark places.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一只手提箱，曾属于某位习惯在暗处持灯探照之人。

aspecteditems.name: Aglaophotis-Scented Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle scented with aglaophotis.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支带有阿格劳福提斯花香味的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Bedside Candleholder
aspecteditems.description: To comfort you through the dark hours.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 在黑暗的时光给你安慰。

aspecteditems.name: Weighty Bedside Candleholder
aspecteditems.description: To comfort you through the dark hours.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 在黑暗的时光给你安慰。

aspecteditems.name: Beeswax Candle
aspecteditems.description: Simple and bright.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 朴素又明亮。

aspecteditems.name: Bottled Candle
aspecteditems.description: An admirable combination of two utterly disparate elements. Quiet genius.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 两种截然不同的元素的完美结合。天才之举。

aspecteditems.name: Chalice Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle scented with fragrant chalice.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支带有香盏花香气的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Historywax Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle made with the oils of the 'history plant', agave aeterna.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一种用“历史植物”，永恒龙舌兰的油制成的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Snowflake Candle
aspecteditems.description: A silver candle soft as snow.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支银色的蜡烛，轻柔如雪。

aspecteditems.name: Widow's Candle
aspecteditems.description: Light it in remembrance.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 将它点燃以作纪念。

aspecteditems.name: Watchful Candle
aspecteditems.description: A little portable clarity.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一盏便携的光源。

aspecteditems.name: Small Candlestick
aspecteditems.description: Simple elegance.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 质朴而优雅。

aspecteditems.name: Tall Candlestick
aspecteditems.description: Elegant simplicity.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 优雅而质朴。

aspecteditems.name: Honeyscar-Scented Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle scented with honeyscar jasmine.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支带有蜜痂茉莉香味的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Moth-Orchid-Scented Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle scented with moth orchid.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支带有蛾兰香味的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Pear-Scented Candle
aspecteditems.description: A candle scented with pyrus auricalcinus.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一支带有 铜梨香味的蜡烛。

aspecteditems.name: Crescent Candelabrum
aspecteditems.description: An iron candelabrum inscribed with a simple frieze of crescent moons.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一只铁质的烛台，上面刻有简单的新月雕饰。

aspecteditems.name: Snowflake Candelabrum
aspecteditems.description: An iron candelabrum inscribed with a simple snowflake symbol.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一只铁质的烛台，上面刻有简单的雪花雕饰。

aspecteditems.name: Ambrose's Favourite Chair
aspecteditems.description: Somewhat pocked with cigar-burns.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 被雪茄烫出了些孔洞。

aspecteditems.name: Staff Armchair
aspecteditems.description: Polished by the posteriors of dozens of loafing prison guards.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 被几十名无所事事的狱警的屁股擦得锃光瓦亮。

aspecteditems.name: Librarian's Armchair
aspecteditems.description: A sea-coloured, star-ornamented armchair.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一把色如海洋，星形花纹的扶手椅。

aspecteditems.name: Grand Reading Armchair
aspecteditems.description: Nestle grandly.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 华丽地安置于此。

aspecteditems.name: Imposing Reading Armchair
aspecteditems.description: Nestle imposingly.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 端庄地安置于此。

aspecteditems.name: Nighted Chair
aspecteditems.description: Solid, comfortable, oddly unobtrusive.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 坚固、舒适、有种奇怪的不起眼。

aspecteditems.name: Kitty's Armchair
aspecteditems.description: This looks very like the armchair in which Kitty Mazarine, second Librarian, sat for El Bretón's famous group portrait.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 它看着很像是在艾尔·布莱顿那张著名的合影里，第二任图书管理员凯蒂·马扎林坐的那把扶手椅。

aspecteditems.name: Baron Silence's Astrolabe
aspecteditems.description: Thomas Dewulf used this armillary - a spherical astrolabe - in his calculations, but it's much older than he was.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 托马斯·德沃尔夫将这架浑天仪——一种球形星盘——用在了自己的计算中，但它可比他古老得多。

aspecteditems.name: Bag of Tricks
aspecteditems.description: 'Useful': a treacherously subjective term. Does this contain anything useful?
aspecteditems.description_cn: “有用”：一个极其主观的词。里边有什么有用的东西吗？

aspecteditems.name: Morgue Boots
aspecteditems.description: Reliable rubber.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 可靠的橡胶。

aspecteditems.name: Lunar Brazier
aspecteditems.description: Scorched by fires lit before even the Romans came.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 甚至早在罗马人到来之前，它就已经在经受火焰的炙烤。

aspecteditems.name: Bucket of Ashes
aspecteditems.description: Long cold, but they faintly remember the fire.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 冷却已久，但它们仍旧隐约记得那火。

aspecteditems.name: Mop and Bucket
aspecteditems.description: Galvanised steel, enriched with the stains of a dozen years of methodical mopping.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 镀锌钢制，上边满是多年来有条不紊的拖地工作留下的污渍。

aspecteditems.name: Bucket of Seawater
aspecteditems.description: Flecks of foam float on the surface.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 细碎的浮沫在水面飘荡。

aspecteditems.name: Bell-Tower Chair
aspecteditems.description: Sturdy, undistinguished, and, like so much else in the House, the last of its kind.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 结实、平凡，而且，正如居屋里的众多物件一样，是仅存的孤品。

aspecteditems.name: Atrium Chair
aspecteditems.description: Reserved for latecomers, non-believers, and the pensive.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 留给迟到者、不信者与忧思者。

aspecteditems.name: Restful Seat
aspecteditems.description: A dawn-coloured seat for a solar congregation.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 用于太阳崇拜集会的拂晓色椅子。

aspecteditems.name: Uncomfortable Seat
aspecteditems.description: Shaped to assure the attention of the faithful.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 为保证信徒能保持集中的注意力而打造。

aspecteditems.name: Contemplative Seat
aspecteditems.description: Perch here to meditate on the mysteries of dawn.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 暂歇于此，冥思拂晓之秘。

aspecteditems.name: Comfortable Garden Chair
aspecteditems.description: Amateurishly varnished, characterfully stained.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 清漆上得外行，色染得倒有个性。

aspecteditems.name: Restful Garden Chair
aspecteditems.description: Sit here and listen to the trees grow. Or the leaves fall. Preferences differ.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 坐在这里聆听树木生长。亦或树叶凋落。人各有所好。

aspecteditems.name: Greene's Red Chair
aspecteditems.description: A little wobbly. Greene used to lean forward.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 有点晃，格林坐在它上面的时候常前倾身子。

aspecteditems.name: Wine-Dark Chair
aspecteditems.description: An elegant eighteenth-century piece imported from France.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一件法国进口的十八世纪优雅之作。

aspecteditems.name: Expansive Chair
aspecteditems.description: Upholstered in a velvet of peculiar richness that invites the hand. Sit down a while. You've earned it.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 用一种异常丰满的丝绒装饰，让人忍不住想用手触摸。坐一会儿吧，你应得的。

aspecteditems.name: Snug Chair
aspecteditems.description: A wicker chair with a soft white lap blanket for chilly evenings.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一张铺着柔软白色膝毯的柳条座椅，为寒冷的夜晚而生。

aspecteditems.name: Chair of Challenges
aspecteditems.description: Here the Librarian Harries sat, to formulate the paradoxes he would bequeath to van Lauren.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 图书管理员哈里斯曾坐在这里，构思他将要留给范·劳伦的悖论。

aspecteditems.name: Straw-Cushioned Chair
aspecteditems.description: Upholstered without any particular skill.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 软垫装得毫无技术含量。

aspecteditems.name: Nightsky Chair
aspecteditems.description: Velvet smooth as midnight.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 丝绒滑如午夜。

aspecteditems.name: Starstrewn Chair
aspecteditems.description: Velvet soft as starlight.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 丝绒柔如星光。

aspecteditems.name: Twilight Chair
aspecteditems.description: Velvet dark as blue dusk.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 丝绒暗如蓝暮。

aspecteditems.name: Severe Chair
aspecteditems.description: Unfussy marsh-green upholstery.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 朴素的沼绿色衬垫。

aspecteditems.name: Spartan Chair
aspecteditems.description: The cushion has been removed, perhaps as an act of petty revenge.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 坐垫被拿走了，也许这是个小气的报复。

aspecteditems.name: Melodic Chair
aspecteditems.description: Someone appears to have tuned the squeaks.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 似乎有人为它的吱呀声调了音。

aspecteditems.name: Lumpy Melodic Chair
aspecteditems.description: Someone appears to have tuned the squeaks.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 似乎有人为它的吱呀声调了音。

aspecteditems.name: Wicker Chair
aspecteditems.description: Elderly, but robust.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 老旧，但结实。

aspecteditems.name: Inviting Footstool
aspecteditems.description: How many home from the storm propped their feet here and gazed into the fire?
aspecteditems.description_cn: 有多少自暴风雨中归家的人儿将双脚搁在它上面，凝望着炉火？

aspecteditems.name: Librarian's Footstool
aspecteditems.description: A sea-coloured, star-ornamented footstool.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一把色如海洋，星形花纹的脚凳。

aspecteditems.name: Moon Footstool
aspecteditems.description: A soft gold glimmer in the half-light.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 柔和的金色朦胧地闪烁着。

aspecteditems.name: Valentine's Memorial
aspecteditems.description: Valentine died two centuries ago. This stone is much newer - more like two decades old.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 瓦伦丁两个世纪前就去世了，这块石头要比那新得多——大约只有二十年的样子。

aspecteditems.name: Elegant Sunburst Lamp
aspecteditems.description: A bright tree of brass.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一株明亮的黄铜树。

aspecteditems.name: Compelling Lamp
aspecteditems.description: Moths circle it like maypole dancers.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 飞蛾如五月柱舞者般绕其盘旋。

aspecteditems.name: Reading Lamp
aspecteditems.description: To ensure clarity of vision even in utmost dark. It does flicker occasionally.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 即便在最为黑暗的情况下也能保证清晰的视野。偶尔会闪烁。

aspecteditems.name: Paradise Palm
aspecteditems.description: An unquenchable vitality.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 一股难以抑制的活力。

aspecteditems.name: Watchful Potted Plant
aspecteditems.description: Not everything needs eyes.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 并非所有存在都需要眼睛。

aspecteditems.name: Lingering Repose
aspecteditems.description: Upholstered in a velvet of peculiar richness that invites the hand.
aspecteditems.description_cn: 用一种异常丰满的丝绒装饰，让人忍不住想用手触摸。

aspecteditems.name: Delightful Repose
aspecteditems.description: Placed by the Curia of the Isle to allow a rest before an ascent. Or after a descent.
